bug_semantics: in_s3 downloads an S3 object and fully materializes the decompressed payload in memory before parsing. Default store_as is gzip; GzipExtractor.extract wraps the object body in Zlib::GzipReader and calls gz.read with no decompressed-size cap (later rewritten to loop concatenated members, still unbounded parts << gz.read / parts.join). gzip_command/lzma2/lzo extractors do the same via Open3.capture2 of gzip/xz/lzop -dc, returning the entire stdout. An attacker who can PUT a highly compressed object into the watched bucket can force Fluentd to expand a small blob into an arbitrarily large string, OOM-kill the process, and stop log collection on the node (CWE-770).
flaw_origin: The unbounded full-buffer decompression path was first written when in_s3 was added: GzipExtractor.extract did Zlib::GzipReader.wrap { |gz| gz.read } and process() assigned content = @extractor.extract(io). That is the smallest public first-write of the missing size limit. Command extractors later copied the same pattern with Open3.capture2; a 2018 concatenated-gzip rewrite kept unbounded gz.read and is not a new origin.
